mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger a flight to safety, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of months when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales growth signal weakening consumer demand, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production, manufacturing sector weakness reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is declining.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPI) indicates inflationary pressures that prompt central bank hawkishness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth and rising unemployment rate indicate a labor market slowdown that reduces consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE does not produce negative 60-day returns in at least 65% of cases, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a low federal funds rate environment (below 0.25%), the market reacts positively to any further rate cuts, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.
